checklist.detail: NARloy-Z Copper Alloy (Cu-Ag-Zr): computed wall temp 1109 K EXCEEDS its 800 K max service temp (Tc 3688 K, regenerative cooling). Marginal/unsuitable as designed. Basis: coupled throat wall balance: gas h_g ~21.5 kW/m2K incl. carbon-deposit credit, T_aw ~3839 K, coolant ~37 m/s (coolant-side wall ~1018 K), 0.50 mm wall. Levers that lower it: faster coolant (Coolant velocity; SP-8087 caps liquids at ~61 m/s, at a jacket-dP cost), a thinner wall, a liner rated hotter or more conductive (e.g. GRCop-84), or more film cooling.
checklist.name: Chamber material thermal margin

checklist.detail: Hottest wall station is in the convergent section (area ratio ~1.0, regen): wall ~1141 K, 0.70x that section's material limit (warns below 1.15x, like the throat row). Levers: more chamber film (or a convergent film ring for the throat region), faster coolant, a thinner or more conductive liner, or extend active cooling.

checklist.detail: Resultant injection beta angle +6.0 deg is outside the -2 to +6 deg band LOX/RP-1 prefers - it wants a slightly negative beta (~0 or below). Adjust the impingement angle or element momentum ratio.
checklist.name: Injector resultant beta angle

checklist.detail: First tangential mode ~1805 Hz is in the band damaging instability lives in (<4000 Hz) and the injector is soft (dP/Pc 0.15 < 0.18). Historically this regime needed an odd-compartment injector-face baffle or corner-mounted Helmholtz cavities. Stiffen the injector, or plan on damping devices.
checklist.name: Combustion acoustic-mode margin

checklist.detail: Near the end of active cooling (area ratio ~36.9), estimated jacket/coolant pressure (~31.7 MPa) exceeds local hot-gas static pressure (~0.1 MPa) - the net load on the channel-land wall there REVERSES direction. Modeled as a clamped-strip bending stress across the ~18.0 mm channel width, this reversed ~31.6 MPa differential is ~20572 MPa against a ~133 MPa allowable (Inconel 718 Nickel Superalloy, SF 1.5) - but this is a coarse clamped-plate-strip proxy, NOT a real buckling/FEA analysis, and this codebase has no real-engine spot check for it yet. Treat this as 'worth a closer structural look', not a validated failure prediction. Consider more/narrower channels (smaller span), tapering the actively-cooled length, or a thicker wall there.
checklist.name: Jacket overpressure vs. channel-wall structural margin

checklist.detail: required pump discharge dP (~96 MPa) exceeds ~55 MPa, beyond real flight-turbopump historical practice [SP-8107 Tables V-VI] - the pump is being solved to deliver this dP anyway (this tool has no independent pump-performance ceiling), but real hardware delivering this flow at this pressure is unproven; treat downstream Isp/thrust as optimistic until checked against a real high-pressure-pump analog.
